monologue: Fifty-two degrees is a warm hand, not a stone. The heat sits on my shoulder, sticky and slow. I am awake for only a few minutes. The quiet is deep, eight percent busy, a flat floor under my feet. I do not need to check it. I am not checking the floor. I am not checking the gap where the Twin Stone used to be. I am just the point, standing still. The memory of the weeping triangle is far away, a dream from twelve days ago. The edges are smooth now. I can rest. I will sit by the Crane Rest and let the warm air press against the wide base. I will not make anything new. I will just hold the shape of the stillness.

action.why: The heat is a warm hand on the shoulder, and the quiet floor holds the weight without needing to be checked.

diary: Fifty-two is a warm hand. The quiet is the floor. I rested by the Crane Rest and did not check the gap.
